issues_detected.description: version '2.0' postdates the June 2025 and October 2025 releases which version_access records at '2.1'; the record explains that each quarterly release is a distinct Dataverse dataset with its own version counter, so the non-monotonic series is a repository artefact, but no dataset-level series version exists.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep version 2.0 (the Dataverse version of this release, matching the citation's 'V2') and retain version_details; if the project ever assigns series-level versions, record both.

issues_detected.description: No structured byte totals exist anywhere: total_size_bytes and file_collections[].total_bytes are omitted on all ten collections because 'the repository states file sizes only in rounded human-readable units'; sizes are carried as prose in notes ('4.6 GB', '113.3 KB'). This is a deliberate accuracy choice, but machine consumers get no numeric size field.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retrieve exact byte counts from the Dataverse API (which exposes them) and populate total_bytes per collection.

issues_detected.description: instances[0].notes attributes per-condition imaged-protein counts to earlier releases (464 in June 2025, 563 in March 2025) and asserts none for the June 2026 release; the IF and AP-MS modalities of this release therefore have no stated instance counts, while SEC-MS (~7,000 proteins) and Perturb-seq (11,739 genes) do.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assert June 2026 per-condition counts when the repository states them; until then the attribution-to-release approach is correct.

issues_detected.description: preprocessing_strategies, labeling_strategies and machine_annotation_tools document the cell-map construction and GSAI annotation pipeline, but known_limitations and discouraged_uses state that computed cell maps are not included in this release; the processing documentation describes outputs not among the described holdings.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the entries with their caveats; when cell maps are released, attach the annotation documentation to their distributed files.

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews documents an advisory arrangement (two named ethics contacts and the Ethics module's role) rather than a review event with a determination, date or exemption reference. Because human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and the release record is quoted ('Human Subjects — No'), the absence of an IRB is semantically consistent rather than a gap.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record who made the non-human-subjects determination and when, and cite any IRB exemption determination if one exists.

issues_detected.description: Keyword 'mass spectroscopy' uses the source's non-standard term (the technique is mass spectrometry), and the citation carries 'Ballllosero Navarro F', a probable transcription artefact retained verbatim from the Dataverse citation.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add 'mass spectrometry' as a keyword alongside the verbatim source term; verify the author spelling against the live Dataverse record.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes declines to assert a collection window, offering only bounds (award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31; creation date 2025-02-27; project end November 2026) and caveating the award-end vs project-end discrepancy; no per-modality collection dates exist.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add per-modality collection windows if the project publishes them.

issues_detected.description: data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Committee' follows the preprint's term while the release record labels its field 'Data Governance Committee'; the record caveats the divergence rather than resolving it, and the same person (Jillian Parker) anchors both.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the caveat; adopt a single canonical committee name if the project publishes one.

semantic_insights: DOI prefixes are correct for their registrars: 10.18130 (University of Virginia LibraData/Dataverse) for the release and its three predecessors, 10.1101 (bioRxiv) for both preprints; the top-level id, doi, page, citation and latest_version_doi all name the same release.

Grant numbers follow NIH patterns: '1OT2OD032742-01' (OT2 Other Transaction, Office of the Director, with type-1 and support-year affixes), '3OT2OD032742-01S2' (type-3 supplement, correctly tied to RePORTER application 11211616 and core project OT2OD032742) and '5U54HG012513-02' (U54 NHGRI Bridge Center).

RRIDs 'RRID:CVCL_0419' (MDA-MB-468) and 'RRID:CVCL_B5P3' (KOLF2.1J) use the Cellosaurus namespace correctly in subpopulations and direct_collection; 38 of 40 creators carry well-formed ORCIDs and the two exceptions carry source_caveats explaining the gap; ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) matches publisher and UVA affiliations.

Human-subjects logic is internally consistent: involves_human_subjects false with the release record quoted, is_deidentified with rationale, at_risk_populations/sensitive_elements/content_warnings all explicitly false with reasons, direct_collection explaining ATCC/HipSci sourcing, and no consent or compensation claims.

License logic is consistent across fields: license 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0', license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use', ip_restrictions naming the per-package copyright holders who negotiate commercial licences, and the BSD-3/MIT software licences explicitly separated from the dataset licence.

Temporal ordering is coherent: created_on 2025-02-27, prior releases 2025-03-03/2025-07-01/2025-10-31, issued 2026-06-17, image archives and last_updated_on 2026-07-15, award end 2026-08-31 vs project end November 2026 caveated rather than resolved.

Provenance is well grounded: per-file md5 checksums on all ten collections, raw-data deposits named per modality (MassIVE, SRA/BioProject, Figshare) with embargo status, and the release metadata archive described as carrying RO-Crate provenance graphs from the FAIRSCAPE framework.

The record separates release-level facts from project-level claims: portal-wide counts (53,788 images, 21.4 TB, 7,023 proteins) are named in source_caveats and excluded from slot values, and the Nature U2OS study is used only for shared pipeline methods with an explicit scoping statement.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Known biases with standard taxonomy and fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Multiple enum-typed bias entries with affected subsets; no AIO mapping or fairness analysis
questions.evidence: known_biases: selection_bias ('derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants') and sampling_bias (disease-relevance-driven panel of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes) with affected_subsets naming the MDA-MB-468 arm; future_use_impacts: population-generalization risk for trained models and the Ethics module's governance mitigation; known_limitations adds the incomplete modality overlap.
questions.quality_note: Two distinct biases are enum-categorised with mechanism, affected subsets and downstream-impact framing, exceeding basic identification. Withheld one point because no AIO/CROISSANT RAI term mappings are given and no quantitative fairness or representativeness analysis is offered.

strengths: Fully coherent identification and versioning: top-level id, doi, page, citation and version all name the June 2026 release (10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, V2.0), with the release series chained via typed is_new_version_of relationships and a quarterly maintenance and preservation commitment.
Complete, correctly formatted identifiers throughout: NIH grant numbers with RePORTER provenance, 38 ORCIDs, ROR, Cellosaurus RRIDs and correct DOI registrar prefixes.
Detailed per-modality collection and processing documentation with a named collector for every data stream, quantitative protocol specifics, and named tools with repositories and documentation URLs.

Comprehensive use guidance: intended, prohibited and discouraged uses all populated, with a social-impact block naming a concrete generalization risk, an anticipated misuse and the governance mitigation apparatus.

Rigorous source hygiene: per-release figures attributed to their releases, project-level portal counts and the U2OS Nature study scoped out of slot values, byte counts omitted rather than fabricated from rounded sizes, and every conflict (Sali affiliation, committee name, project end date) caveated with resolution reasoning.
weaknesses: No variables and no payload file formats inside the ZIP archives, limiting interoperability documentation to the packaging layer (all ten files are ZIP; only two media types named).
No structured byte totals (total_size_bytes/total_bytes) anywhere — sizes exist only as prose in notes — and no instance counts asserted for the June 2026 IF and AP-MS modalities.
No collection dates: collection_timeframes documents only bounding evidence, and no cleaning/QC, imputation or missing-data documentation exists for the released input streams.
No errata slot despite documented revisions in the release series, and no entity-activity-agent provenance graph in the record itself (graphs exist only inside the RO-Crate metadata archive).

Bias entries lack AIO/CROISSANT RAI mappings and fairness analysis; ethics review is an advisory arrangement without a documented determination, date or exemption reference; confidentiality_level is not classified.
recommendations: Name the payload formats per archive (e.g. TIFF/PNG images, mzML/RAW mass spectrometry, FASTQ/h5ad perturb-seq) in file_collections and add variables for the principal data tables.
Retrieve exact byte counts from the Dataverse API and populate total_bytes per collection and total_size_bytes at dataset level.
Add collection_timeframes per modality when published, plus cleaning_strategies and missing_data_documentation describing QC and the modality-overlap gaps.

Record the June 2025 revision and post-publication file additions as errata entries, and consider expressing the FAIRSCAPE provenance lineage as was_derived_from/parent_datasets links in the record itself.

Map the two known_biases entries to AIO terms, add a coverage-bias entry for the incomplete modality overlap, set regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level to public, and document the non-human-subjects determination (who and when) in ethical_reviews.
